name: Wenns
kurzbeschreibung: High-altitude village in the Pitztal valley, featuring the Hochzeiger ski area and a traditional town center surrounded by the Pitztaler mountain landscape.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The municipality of Wenns is situated at an elevation of 962 metres above sea level in the front Pitztal valley within the Imst district of Tyrol. This sun-drenched alpine village rests upon an expansive hillside terrace above the Pitze river, serving as the geographic and cultural heart of the lower valley where the road branches towards the inner glacier valley and across the Piller Sattel pass into the neighbouring Kaunertal. Home to approximately 2,150 residents, the community encompasses numerous historic hamlets, climbing from 820 metres on the valley floor to the summit of Mount Venet at 2,512 metres. As the gateway to the Kaunergrat Nature Park, Wenns seamlessly blends living Tyrolean heritage with pristine alpine wilderness, boasting centuries of judicial tradition and international renown as the cradle of crib-carving schools.

Geschichte

Prehistoric discoveries, including a Bronze Age sacrificial site at the nearby Piller Sattel, prove that this mountain corridor has served as a vital alpine pass for millennia. The village was first documented around 1150 in the annals of Marienberg Abbey in South Tyrol. During the late Middle Ages, Wenns occupied an exceptional administrative standing in North Tyrol with its own autonomous village bailiwick and local magistracy, a heritage commemorated by the judicial rod on the municipal coat of arms. Tree-ring analysis identified the village's 'Doppelsitzer-Haus' as the oldest dated timber farmhouse in North Tyrol, dating back to the 13th century. On the village square stands the historic Platzhaus, rebuilt in 1576 with remarkable Renaissance facade frescoes. The parish church dedicated to Saint John the Baptist was reconstructed in the early 17th century following a fire and enlarged around 1790. In 1860, the world's very first nativity-scene carving school was founded here.

Anreise

Wenns benefits from straightforward transport links within western Tyrol. Motorists leave the Inntal Autobahn A12 at the Imst/Pitztal exit or travel toll-free from southern Germany along the B179 Fernpass highway via Nassereith and Imst. From Imst, the Pitztal provincial road L16 leads directly into Wenns, while the scenic L17 ascends across the Piller Sattel. Rail passengers arrive at Imst-Pitztal railway station on the main Arlberg line, served by domestic and international express trains. From the station forecourt, frequent VVT regional bus services (line 310) connect directly to Wenns village centre and surrounding stops. Overnight guests holding the local valley card enjoy complimentary public transport throughout the entire Pitztal valley.

Tipps

A premier regional attraction is the Kaunergrat Nature Park House situated at the 1,559-metre Piller Sattel pass: the cantilevered 'Gachenblick' viewing terrace offers a breathtaking sheer 800-metre drop overlooking the Inn and Kauner valleys, complemented by an interactive alpine multimedia exhibition. Immediately below lies the Piller Moor nature reserve, traversed by a barrier-free timber boardwalk leading through rare peat bog flora to an 11-metre observation tower. Heritage lovers should admire the 16th-century Renaissance facade of the Platzhaus on the main square and visit the local nativity craft exhibitions. In summer, the sunny southern flanks of Mount Venet (2,512 m) offer rewarding panoramic hikes, while winter brings family-friendly skiing and prepared cross-country ski trails.
